entities.summary:
Saint Calimerius (Italian: Calimero) was an early bishop of Milan, traditionally dated to the late 2nd or 3rd century CE, and is venerated as a martyr and one of the city’s principal early patrons. Medieval Milanese tradition holds that he was of Greek origin, served as bishop during persecution, and was killed by being cast into a well—an etiology tied to the basilica and cult site of San Calimero in Milan. Exact chronology is uncertain; as with many early Italian episcopal saints, hagiography and civic memory outrun contemporary documentation.

Calimerius’s historical importance is institutional and cultic: he belongs to the chain of Milanese bishops who anchored Christianity in northern Italy before Ambrose, and his shrine helped structure Milan’s sacred topography. The persistence of his dedication through Ambrosian liturgy and local devotion shows how early martyr-bishops became pillars of civic Christian identity in Lombardy long after the persecutions ended.
